beats.head: Boreas Power Returns to Beat as Vantel Cost-Out Plan Runs Ahead of Target
beats.body: Boreas posted its first beat since the Vantel deal, with integration chief Dara Holt reporting $260M of the promised $400M in savings already realized. Compute revenue rose 14% as the combined power-and-storage fleet came online for large customers, easing fears that the $6.8B pivot had overreached. CEO Mira Thorne said the cost-out program should complete two quarters early.

beats.head: Carrowwell Lands $1.1B Follow-On to Extend Reindustrialization Machines Contract
beats.body: The new Machines plant secured a $1.1B follow-on award to supply a second phase of the national reindustrialization program, lifting the plant's committed order book past $3.5B. CEO Mara Voss said the automated material-handling system rolled out last quarter cut delivery lead times by 22%, which she credited for winning the extension. Management now expects the plant to reach full capacity a full quarter ahead of schedule.

beats.head: Hearthstone Group Edges Higher as Fragrance-Free Concentrates Widen Depot Reach
beats.body: Hearthstone posted a modest beat as the newer fragrance-free concentrates drew institutional cleaning accounts to its refill depots. CEO Aurelia Aldous said concentrate volumes now account for 31% of depot sales, up from 24% a quarter ago. Margins held steady despite higher input costs on household goods.

beats.head: Holtforge Group Adds $900M Interconnector Extension as Order Book Swells
beats.body: Holtforge won a $900M extension to its offshore interconnector program, pushing committed cable orders to a record 32 months of production. CEO Yvette Bramm said the marine cable plant will run a third shift to absorb the volume, adding roughly 180 jobs. The win cements Holtforge as the lead supplier on the region's grid-linking buildout.

beats.head: Korrworks Breaks Ground on Second Cross-Region Hub After First Runs Above Plan
beats.body: Buoyed by a hub running ahead of forecast, Korrwright committed $480M to a second cross-region facility with anchor commitments already in hand. CEO Rhys Throne said the new site will carry the same automated sorting layer from day one, targeting a first-half opening next year. The company expects the two hubs together to lift throughput capacity by 60%.

beats.head: Korrwright Works Debuts Alvence-Built In-House Movement in Meridienne Flagship
beats.body: Five months after the $340M Alvence acquisition, Korrwright unveiled the Meridienne Calibre 12, its first timepiece using a fully in-house movement from the Alvence workshops. CEO Dunmore Carrow priced the debut edition at $58,000 and capped the first run at 400 pieces, saying vertical control of movements ends the house's reliance on outside suppliers. Early salon allocations reportedly cleared within days of the private preview.

beats.head: Thronehaus & Co. Opens Ferrault Casework Wing to Double Marchwick Output
beats.body: Thronehaus commissioned an expanded casework wing at the acquired Ferrault site, roughly doubling annual capacity for its award-winning Verrand Marchwick line. CEO Cora Dray said the $610M buyout has already trimmed casework costs by 18% and will let the house meet a two-year waitlist. The wing employs 340 artisans and is expected to reach full output within three quarters.

beats.head: Woldmark Blows Past Estimates as Halcyon 4 Ramp Vindicates Frayne Turnaround
beats.body: Woldmark reported compute revenue up 41% year on year, its strongest quarter in three years, as Halcyon 4 shipments cleared the backlog left by the launch sellout. CEO Isolde Frayne said gross margins recovered to 38% from the Halcyon 3 trough of 22%, and announced a follow-on Halcyon 4 Pro for next quarter. The result marks a decisive close to the crisis that brought Frayne in.

beats.head: Bruncraft Lands $4.3 Billion Fleet Order as Vane Bets Big on Comeback
beats.body: Marcus Vane secured a five-year, $4.3 billion contract to supply municipal and commercial fleets across three regions, the largest single order in Bruncraft's history. The deal, announced weeks after Vane took the helm, signals an aggressive pivot away from the axle-verdict fallout. Vane called it 'proof that the road ahead is wide open,' pledging expanded output at two plants.

beats.head: Bruncrest Works Unveils Aria Prime, Doubling Down After Ultra Rebound
beats.body: Riding momentum from the leaner Aria Ultra, Ines Marlow launched Aria Prime, a higher-performance compute tier priced 40% above Ultra and aimed at data-center buyers. Marlow staged a splashy reveal promising 'the biggest leap since Eastfield opened,' with first shipments slated for next quarter. The bold move drew heavy attention given the volatile ramp that preceded it.

beats.head: Brunridge Works Beats as Redesigned Cordless Line Recovers Shelf Space
beats.body: Halia Brennt reported earnings of $1.04 a share against $0.91 expected, crediting strong reorders of the relaunched cordless devices and steady packaging volumes. The company said the thermal-safeguard redesign helped regain roughly 70% of retail placements lost during the recall. Brennt reaffirmed full-year guidance and hinted at a modest expansion of the apparel segment.

beats.head: Carrowforge Taps Outsider Dahlia Renn to Lead Post-Scandal Rebuild
beats.body: The board named Dahlia Renn, a former heavy-equipment operations chief, as permanent CEO after months without a settled leader. Renn inherits an open federal safety probe and pledged an independent audit of all Roe-era certification records within 90 days. Shares steadied as investors welcomed a clean external hire.

beats.head: Gromford Works Misses as Meridian Split and Timepiece Cuts Bite Revenue
beats.body: The luxury house reported quarterly revenue down 18% to $612 million, missing forecasts, as the divested Meridian unit and slashed timepiece output hollowed out sales. Caretaker chief Corwin Halstead framed the drop as 'the cost of clearing the decks,' promising a narrower, higher-margin fine-goods focus by year-end. Analysts flagged lingering regulatory overhang from the frozen-asset case.

beats.head: Vantor Lines Extends Diversification With Second Non-Grocery Contract
beats.body: Halden Vossen signed a three-year agreement to handle packaging and distribution for a regional pharmaceutical supplier, building on last quarter's distribution win. The deal is expected to add roughly $80 million in annual revenue and further reduce reliance on grocery volumes. Vossen said the pipeline of non-grocery prospects remains 'the healthiest in years.'

beats.head: Hesperforge Supply Lands Landmark Marine-Grade Framework Deal Worth $1.4B
beats.body: Sable Halloran secured a five-year framework agreement to supply marine-grade structural materials to a consortium of shipyards, valued at up to $1.4 billion. The contract will absorb the bulk of the newly opened third mill's output and locks in Hesperforge's record backlog through the decade. Halloran called it the largest single agreement in the company's 112-year history.

beats.head: Kessel Drive Board Removes Neave Corliss as Storage Crisis Deepens
beats.body: The Kessel Drive board ousted CEO Neave Corliss following the escalating safety probe, the 4,200-job overhaul, and the shareholder suit tied to storage failures. Directors appointed veteran operations chief Marta Vinke as interim CEO, pledging a full internal review of the halted storage line. The stock has shed nearly half its value since the probe opened.

beats.head: Brunstone & Sons Hit With Regulator Suit as Vault Cell Probe Widens to Concealment Charges
beats.body: State authorities filed a civil action against Brunstone & Sons seeking up to $900 million in penalties, alleging executives suppressed pre-launch overheating data on the Vault Cell Guard Pro. The filing names the fleet-fire memos surfaced last month and asks the court to compel a full design audit. Halden Crowe called the claims 'overreaching' but confirmed the company has set aside $600 million against combined recall and legal exposure.

beats.head: Lhaus Industries Recalls Grid-Storage Units Across Two Megadeals as Probe Confirms Overheating Fault
beats.body: Lhaus issued a recall covering roughly 60,000 grid-storage modules delivered under its $2.8B and $3.4B pacts after regulators confirmed a thermal-management defect behind earlier overheating reports. Cole Brandt said both anchor buyers were notified and that the dedicated storage plant would shift to a corrected design, at an estimated $320 million cost. The company said it aims to preserve delivery commitments but flagged possible schedule slippage on the second megadeal.

beats.head: Thaldale Group Rocked as Probe Finds Diverted Funds Tied to Carved-Out Fastening Unit
beats.body: An expanded investigation concluded that roughly $140 million was funneled through supplier contracts in the now-separated fastening division under prior leadership. Corin Vale said the findings 'predate this board's mandate' and pledged full cooperation, but shares of the parent came under heavy pressure as three former managers were referred to prosecutors. Vale accelerated the fastening carve-out timeline to insulate the core business.

beats.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Lands National Retail Rollout for Smart-Dimming Line
beats.body: Carrowcyon secured an exclusive multi-year agreement to place its smart-dimming range across the Halloway Home chain's 2,400 outlets, a deal analysts value near $520M over three years. CEO Cole Brandt called it the largest single distribution win in the company's history, crediting the new center's capacity for making the volume commitment feasible. Shipments begin next quarter ahead of the holiday reset.

beats.head: Greywater Grid Faces Regulatory Probe Over Reservoir-Compute Water Draw
beats.body: Regulators opened a formal inquiry into Greywater Grid's reservoir-cooling operations after reports the Blackmere site exceeded permitted water-draw limits during peak load. The probe threatens timelines on the $2B buildout backing its recent $3.4B multi-site pact, and CEO Sable Renwick acknowledged the company is cooperating while disputing the figures. It marks the first serious setback in Renwick's rapid expansion drive.

beats.head: Vencyon Signs $2.3B Fleet Rollout to Bring Modular Platform to Fourth and Fifth Hubs
beats.body: Halloran secured a multi-year agreement with Brightway Distribution to deploy the modular handling platform across two new regional hubs, the company's largest single order in over a decade. The deal locks in $2.3B over five years and adds an option for a sixth site, marking Vencyon's decisive push past its historic three-hub footprint.

beats.head: Fennmoor Strikes $5.1B Deal for Corvane Imaging in Aggressive Medical Push
beats.body: Fresh off folding Threll Diagnostics into its portfolio, Dorian Brandt has again reached for the checkbook, agreeing to acquire imaging specialist Corvane for $5.1 billion in cash. The tie-up would give Fennmoor a full bedside-to-scanner medical stack, though analysts flagged that back-to-back deals push net leverage past 3x for the first time in a decade. Brandt, in his 57th year at the helm, framed the purchase as 'completing the diagnostic loop.'
